findings.failure_path: main appends receipt exclusion pathspecs to paths and then passes that filtered tuple to require_committed_tree. After committing an added receipt, modify that receipt without committing: git status receives its exclude pathspec, reports clean, and the gate continues despite dirty evidence. Any later evidence read from the working tree can therefore validate bytes that will not land, while a clean merge-side run sees the committed receipt instead.
findings.smallest_fix: Run require_committed_tree against the original unfiltered scope (normally all paths) before adding receipt exclusion pathspecs; use the filtered paths only for candidate diff/hash computation. Add a regression test that dirties a committed added receipt and requires the uncommitted-changes refusal.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: The committed-tree fix is incomplete: the same receipt pathspecs excluded from candidate hashing are also excluded from the dirty-tree check, contradicting the recorded claim that dirty evidence is refused.

A caller can modify an added receipt after committing it and still pass require_committed_tree; this leaves evidence evaluation exposed to working-tree state and can produce a local false green or an unreproducible CI result.
